title: Personal Checking: Dispute Notice and Provisional Credit Deadlines and the New-Account Period
content:
## Figures covered

Personal Checking uses one set of time figures for electronic-transaction disputes and for the treatment of newly opened accounts:

- **Notice window** — how many calendar days, counted from the posting of a disputed debit, the owner has to give notice if the claim is to go through the electronic dispute process.
- **Provisional credit deadline** — how many business days, counted from the owner's notice, may run on a still-open dispute before a provisional credit becomes owed.
- **New-account provisional credit deadline** — the longer business-day count substituted for the ordinary one when, on the notice date, the account had been open for fewer days than the new-account period.
- **New-account period** — how many calendar days from opening an account is treated as new, which affects both check holds and dispute deadlines.
- **New-account check hold** — for an account still inside that period, the business day, counted from the deposit, on which a deposited check is credited and its funds may be used.

## Values

| Tier | Notice window (calendar days) | Provisional credit deadline (business days) | New-account deadline (business days) | New-account period (calendar days) | New-account check hold (business day after deposit) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 5 |
| Student Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 5 |
| Everyday Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 5 |
| Interest Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 5 |
| Premier Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 5 |
| Private Client Checking | 120 | 10 | 20 | 30 | 5 |

## Observation

These five figures are identical across all six tiers, so the tier held never alters them. Whether the longer provisional credit deadline or the new-account check hold comes into play turns on the account's age against the 30-day new-account period, not on its tier.

Hypothetical comparison: a dispute noticed on an account opened 12 calendar days earlier runs on the 20-business-day deadline, while one noticed on an account opened a year earlier runs on the 10-business-day deadline.
